findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2391-2395 — HIGH: the public `lattice dispatch --help` contract still says dispatch is only for one item/finding/cluster and tells users to provide exactly one item identifier, even though the new registry deliberately supports story-only reviewer dispatches. This preserves the original C4 guidance/handler disagreement: a reviewer following help can add itemId and then be rejected by the story-only runtime contract. packages/main/src/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.ts:127-150 does not catch it because it requires the stale item/finding/cluster wording and validates each field separately instead of validating complete registry-derived example payloads/help semantics. Fix the catalog descriptions to explain conditional story-only vs exactly-one cardinality, and add a test that fails on the current help text and validates complete examples against the public command schema/runtime contract.

packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:418 and packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:472 / :745 — HIGH: the registry exposes a denied-command matrix, but real handler enforcement is wired only into checklist_update. finding_add never calls assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed (it uses a lattice-review-* prefix), and finding_resolve ignores actor/LATTICE_AGENT entirely. Thus LATTICE_AGENT=test-intent can write a finding and LATTICE_AGENT=lattice-review-quality can resolve one even though both commands are denied by their registry rows. The smoke exhaustively tests the pure helper but exercises only two selected real consumers, so it cannot prove the documented claim that permittedMutations is mechanically enforced. Wire the registry authorization into every declared mutation consumer (with deliberate main/unclassified-host compatibility) and add handler-level allow/deny coverage for every command class.

packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2391-2395 — MEDIUM: the public dispatch help still says the command is only for one item/finding/cluster and that itemId should provide exactly one target, even though the new registry accepts story-only reviewer/delivery calls. `node packages/main/dist/cli.js dispatch --help` reproduces the contradictory contract, and command-catalog-smoke currently asserts the stale description instead of the new story-level behavior. Update description/argument guidance and make the smoke require story-only wording so the user-facing contract matches the handler and transition hints.

packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:418-431 and packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:559-577 — HIGH: the registry mutation matrix is not wired into all declared command consumers. `assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed` is called only by checklist_update; review-run separately uses lane classification, while finding_add/review_pass_set/finding_resolve/init_check_set/scope_check_save/delivery_check_set do not consume the registry mutation authority (several do not even accept an actor). The exhaustive smoke at agent-dispatch-registry-smoke.ts:209-223 tests only the pure helper, so it can pass while real handlers permit registry-denied actors/commands. This contradicts CHK-002 adversarial:1 and the L4 process-fact claim that role-gated mutation consumers enforce the shared registry. Wire each gate-relevant mutation entry through a fail-closed registered actor check (preserving explicitly intended human/main paths), and add real-handler negative tests that compare story/checklist/evidence state before and after every denied class.
